title: First Fleet arrives in Australia
summary: Eleven British ships carrying about 1,400 people, more than half of them convicts, arrive at Botany Bay and move on to Sydney Cove, where Captain Arthur Phillip founds a penal colony. The land is already home to Aboriginal peoples, including the Eora, whose ancestors have lived in Australia for at least 50,000 years.
significance: The colony began British settlement of Australia, which brought devastating losses of land and life to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples; 26 January is now Australia Day and, for many, also a day of mourning.

zh.title: 第一舰队抵达澳大利亚
zh.summary: 十一艘英国船载约一千四百人，其中逾半为囚犯，抵达植物湾后转至悉尼湾，建立流放殖民地。当地原住民包括埃奥拉人，其祖先已在澳大利亚生活至少五万年。
zh.significance: 殖民带来原住民土地与生命的巨大损失。1月26日成为澳大利亚国庆，也被许多人视为哀悼日。

title: French Revolution
summary: With France bankrupt, King Louis XVI calls the Estates-General, and the deputies of the commoners declare themselves a National Assembly. Parisians storm the Bastille fortress on 14 July, and the Assembly abolishes feudal privileges and issues the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.
significance: Over the next decade the revolution abolished the monarchy, executed the king, went through the Terror and spread through war, and its ideals of liberty, equality and national sovereignty reshaped politics around the world.

zh.title: 法国大革命
zh.summary: 财政危机迫使路易十六召开三级会议，平民代表宣布组成国民议会。巴黎民众于7月14日攻占巴士底狱，议会随后废除封建特权，发表《人权与公民权宣言》。
zh.significance: 此后革命废黜并处死国王，经历恐怖统治和战争，其自由、平等与国民主权理念改变世界政治。

title: Qajar Iran
summary: The Qajars, a Turkic tribal dynasty, reunited Iran after decades of civil war and made Tehran the capital. They lost the Caucasus to Russia, came under growing Russian and British pressure, and were forced by a popular movement to grant a constitution and parliament in 1906.
significance: Under the Qajars Iran kept its independence between two empires, and the constitutional revolution of 1906 began its modern politics.

zh.title: 伊朗卡扎尔王朝
zh.summary: 突厥部落出身的卡扎尔王朝在数十年内战后统一伊朗，定都德黑兰。它将高加索领土丢给俄国，并承受英俄日增的压力。1906年，民众运动迫使王朝接受宪法与议会。
zh.significance: 卡扎尔时期伊朗在两大帝国之间维持独立，1906年立宪革命则开启了现代政治。

title: Dream of the Red Chamber published
summary: The novel by Cao Xueqin, who died in poverty in the 1760s leaving it unfinished, is printed for the first time in a 120-chapter version completed by other hands. It follows the decline of a great aristocratic family through the eyes of its young heir and the women around him.
significance: It is generally regarded as the greatest Chinese novel, with a whole field of scholarship devoted to it.

zh.title: 《红楼梦》刊行
zh.summary: 曹雪芹于18世纪60年代贫困中去世，留下未完成的小说。后来经他人补成的一百二十回本首次付印。全书通过年轻继承人及周围女性的命运，描绘贵族大家庭的衰落。
zh.significance: 《红楼梦》被广泛视为中国最伟大的小说，并形成了专门研究它的“红学”。

title: Haitian Revolution
summary: Enslaved Africans in the French colony of Saint-Domingue, the richest sugar colony in the Caribbean, rise in revolt. Under leaders such as Toussaint Louverture and Jean-Jacques Dessalines, they defeat French, Spanish and British forces, including an army sent by Napoleon, and declare the independent nation of Haiti on 1 January 1804.
significance: Haiti became the second independent country in the Americas, after the United States, and a state founded by formerly enslaved people, which inspired the enslaved and alarmed slaveholders across the Atlantic world.

zh.title: 海地革命
zh.summary: 法国圣多明各殖民地的非洲奴隶起义，在杜桑·卢维杜尔、德萨林等人领导下击败法国、西班牙与英国军队，1804年1月1日宣布海地独立。
zh.significance: 海地成为美洲第二个独立国家，也是前奴隶建立的国家，鼓舞受奴役者并震动大西洋世界的奴隶主。

title: Macartney Embassy to China
summary: Lord Macartney, sent by Britain to ask for wider trade and a permanent ambassador in Beijing, is received by the Qianlong Emperor at his summer residence. The emperor refuses every request, writing to King George III that China has no need of Britain's manufactures.
significance: The failure showed how differently the two empires saw the world, and Britain's wish to open China's trade led within fifty years to the Opium War.

zh.title: 马戛尔尼使团访华
zh.summary: 英国派马戛尔尼请求扩大贸易、在北京常驻使节。乾隆皇帝在避暑山庄接见他，却拒绝全部要求，并致信乔治三世，表示中国无须英国制品。
zh.significance: 失败暴露出两国世界观的差异。英国迫使中国扩大贸易的企图，在不到五十年后引向鸦片战争。
zh.locationName: 承德（皇帝避暑山庄所在地）

title: Sikh Empire
summary: Ranjit Singh united the Sikh warrior bands of the Punjab, took Lahore in 1799 and built a kingdom reaching from the Khyber Pass to Kashmir, with an army trained by European officers. After his death in 1839 the state fell into disorder, and the British annexed it after two wars.
significance: It was the last large independent state in India to fall to the British.

zh.title: 锡克帝国
zh.summary: 兰吉特·辛格统一旁遮普锡克武装，1799年占领拉合尔，建立从开伯尔山口至克什米尔的王国，以欧洲军官训练军队。1839年去世后内乱，英国经两次战争吞并。
zh.significance: 它是印度最后一个被英国征服的大型独立国家。

title: Dutch East Indies
summary: When the Dutch East India Company went bankrupt, the Dutch state took over its possessions in the Indonesian archipelago and extended its rule over the islands during the 19th century. The colony exported coffee, sugar, rubber and oil until Japan occupied it in 1942.
significance: Dutch rule drew together the many islands and peoples that became Indonesia, which won its independence in 1949.

zh.title: 荷属东印度
zh.summary: 荷兰东印度公司破产后，荷兰政府接管群岛领地，并于19世纪扩展统治。殖民地输出咖啡、糖、橡胶和石油，直到1942年被日本占领。
zh.significance: 荷兰统治将众多岛屿与族群联系起来，成为1949年取得独立的印度尼西亚。

title: Napoleonic Wars
summary: Napoleon's France fought shifting European coalitions in wars that redrew borders and mobilized large armies. His final defeat at Waterloo and the Congress of Vienna established a new European settlement.
significance: The wars spread the legal and administrative reforms of the French Revolution across Europe, stirred nationalism, and left Britain the leading world power for a century.

zh.title: 拿破仑战争
zh.summary: 拿破仑法国与不断变化的欧洲联盟交战，动员庞大军队并重划疆界。滑铁卢战败与维也纳会议最终建立新的欧洲秩序。
zh.significance: 战争传播法国革命的法律行政改革，激发民族主义，并使英国在此后一百年成为领先世界强国。

title: First French Empire
summary: Napoleon Bonaparte, a general who had seized power in France in 1799, crowned himself emperor in 1804. His armies defeated Austria, Prussia and Russia and at their height controlled most of the European continent, before the invasion of Russia in 1812 destroyed them. He was finally defeated at Waterloo in 1815.
significance: Napoleon's law code and administrative reforms outlasted his empire and were adopted across Europe and beyond.

zh.title: 法兰西第一帝国
zh.summary: 1799年掌权的拿破仑于1804年称帝，军队击败奥地利、普鲁士和俄国，鼎盛时控制欧洲大陆大部。1812年侵俄损失惨重，1815年终于滑铁卢败亡。
zh.significance: 拿破仑法典与行政改革比帝国更为持久，被欧洲及世界多地采纳。

title: Latin American wars of independence
summary: With Spain occupied by Napoleon, local leaders across Spanish America set up their own governments from 1810, and long wars with Spanish forces follow. Led by figures such as Simón Bolívar in the north, José de San Martín in the south and, in Mexico, at first the priest Miguel Hidalgo, most of the mainland colonies win independence by 1826, while Brazil breaks away from Portugal in 1822.
significance: New countries including Mexico, Colombia, Venezuela, Peru, Chile and Argentina replaced three centuries of Spanish rule, though many inherited deep social inequalities and soon faced civil wars and military strongmen.

zh.title: 拉丁美洲独立战争
zh.summary: 拿破仑占领西班牙后，美洲殖民地自1810年起建立本地政府，并在玻利瓦尔、圣马丁、伊达尔戈等人领导下争取独立。到1826年，大陆多数殖民地独立，巴西则于1822年脱离葡萄牙。
zh.significance: 墨西哥、哥伦比亚、秘鲁等新国家取代三百年殖民统治，却继承深刻不平等，并常陷入内战和军事强人统治。
zh.locationName: 加拉加斯（代表地点；玻利瓦尔出生地）

title: Waterloo and the Congress of Vienna
summary: Napoleon, back from exile, is finally defeated by British, Dutch, German and Prussian armies at Waterloo, in today's Belgium, in June 1815. At the Congress of Vienna, which finishes its work days before the battle, the victorious powers redraw the map of Europe, restoring old monarchies and seeking a balance of power.
significance: The settlement helped keep peace among Europe's great powers for decades, with no general European war until 1914, though it held back nationalist and liberal movements.

zh.title: 滑铁卢战役与维也纳会议
zh.summary: 拿破仑自流放地返回后，1815年6月在滑铁卢最终败于英、荷、德与普鲁士军。战役前数日结束的维也纳会议已决定恢复旧王朝、重划欧洲并维持均势。
zh.significance: 这一安排维系大国间数十年和平，直到1914年才再爆发全欧战争，但也压制民族与自由主义运动。

title: Zulu Kingdom
summary: Shaka became chief of the small Zulu clan in 1816 and, with new weapons, tactics and discipline, built a kingdom that dominated southeastern Africa, setting off wars and migrations across the region. In 1879 a Zulu army destroyed a British force at Isandlwana, but the kingdom was defeated later that year and annexed in 1897.
significance: The rise of the Zulu reshaped the peoples of southern Africa, and their resistance became a lasting source of pride.

zh.title: 祖鲁王国
zh.summary: 沙卡1816年成为祖鲁首领，以新战术、武器和纪律建立主导非洲东南部的王国，引发广泛战争与迁徙。1879年祖鲁军在伊散德尔瓦纳重创英军，却于同年败亡，1897年被吞并。
zh.significance: 祖鲁崛起重塑南部非洲社会，其抵抗也成为持久的民族自豪来源。

title: First Opium War
summary: When the Chinese official Lin Zexu destroys over a thousand tonnes of opium smuggled into Canton by British merchants, Britain sends warships. Its navy, including steam-powered gunboats, wins easily, and the Treaty of Nanjing forces China to pay compensation, open five ports to trade and give Hong Kong Island to Britain.
significance: It was the first of what Chinese call the 'unequal treaties' that opened China to Western powers on their terms, the start of what is often called China's 'century of humiliation'.

zh.title: 第一次鸦片战争
zh.summary: 林则徐销毁英国商人走私到广州的千余吨鸦片后，英国派遣军舰。英军凭借包括蒸汽炮舰在内的海军优势获胜。《南京条约》迫使清朝赔款、开放五口通商，并割让香港岛。
zh.significance: 这是中国所称“不平等条约”体系的开端，常被视为“百年国耻”的起点。

title: Treaty of Waitangi
summary: Representatives of the British Crown and over 40 Māori chiefs sign a treaty at Waitangi, in New Zealand's Bay of Islands, and copies are later signed by around 500 more chiefs. The English and Māori-language versions differ: in the English text the chiefs give up sovereignty, while the Māori text grants the British governance but guarantees the chiefs' full authority over their lands and treasures.
significance: The treaty is regarded as New Zealand's founding document, and disputes over its meaning and breaches, especially land seizures, remain central to the country's politics.

zh.title: 《怀唐伊条约》
zh.summary: 英国代表与四十余毛利首领签约，后来又有约五百位首领签署。英文称让渡主权，毛利文本则授予治理权，同时保障首领对土地与珍宝的权威，两种文本含义不同。
zh.significance: 条约被视为新西兰建国文件，对其解释和土地侵占等违约行为的争议，至今仍是政治核心议题。

title: Revolutions of 1848 and the Communist Manifesto
summary: A wave of revolutions sweeps across Europe, starting in Sicily and Paris and spreading to the German states, the Austrian Empire and Italy, as liberals, nationalists and workers demand constitutions, national unity and reform. The same year Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels publish The Communist Manifesto in London, calling on the workers of the world to unite.
significance: Most of the revolutions were crushed within a year or two, but they ended the French monarchy and serfdom in the Austrian Empire, and the Manifesto became one of the most influential political texts of modern times.

zh.title: 1848年革命与《共产党宣言》
zh.summary: 革命从西西里、巴黎蔓延至德意志、奥地利和意大利，自由派、民族主义者与劳工要求宪法、统一及改革。同年马克思、恩格斯在伦敦发表《共产党宣言》。
zh.significance: 多数革命很快失败，却终结法国君主制和奥地利农奴制；《宣言》则成为近代最具影响的政治文本之一。

title: Taiping Rebellion
summary: The Taiping movement challenged the Qing dynasty and established a rival state based in Nanjing. The resulting civil war devastated large parts of China and severely strained Qing rule.
significance: It was one of the deadliest wars in history, with perhaps 20 million or more dead, and it fatally weakened the Qing dynasty.

zh.title: 太平天国运动
zh.summary: 太平天国反抗清朝，以南京为都建立对立政权。长期内战破坏中国大片地区，严重削弱清廷统治。
zh.significance: 这场战争可能造成两千万或更多人死亡，是历史上最惨烈的战争之一，并使清朝元气大伤。

title: Perry's ships open Japan

location.name: Uraga, at the mouth of Edo Bay

summary: Commodore Matthew Perry of the United States Navy anchors four warships, two of them steamers, off Uraga and delivers a letter demanding that Japan open its ports. He returns the next year with a larger squadron, and the shogunate signs a treaty opening two ports to American ships.
significance: The treaties that followed ended Japan's seclusion and discredited the shogunate, leading to its overthrow in the Meiji Restoration fifteen years later.

zh.title: 佩里舰队打开日本国门
zh.summary: 美国海军准将佩里率四艘军舰，其中两艘为蒸汽舰，驶抵浦贺，递交要求日本开港的国书。次年他率更大舰队返回，幕府签约，向美国船只开放两处港口。
zh.significance: 随后的一系列条约结束日本锁国，削弱幕府威信，并在十五年后引向明治维新。

title: Second Opium War
summary: Britain and France go to war with Qing China to force wider trade and diplomatic access. Their troops take Guangzhou and Tianjin, march on Beijing in 1860 and loot and burn the emperor's Old Summer Palace. China is made to legalize the opium trade, open more ports, admit foreign envoys to the capital and cede Kowloon to Britain.
significance: The defeat, while the Taiping Rebellion was still raging, exposed the weakness of the Qing and deepened foreign control over China's trade.

zh.title: 第二次鸦片战争
zh.summary: 英国与法国对清朝发动战争，要求扩大贸易与外交准入。联军攻占广州、天津，1860年进军北京，劫掠并焚毁圆明园。清朝被迫将鸦片贸易合法化、增开口岸、准许公使驻京并割让九龙。
zh.significance: 太平天国战争尚未结束时的这次失败，进一步暴露清朝的虚弱，加深了外国对中国贸易的控制。

title: Indian Rebellion of 1857
summary: Indian soldiers (sepoys) of the East India Company's army mutiny at Meerut, angered partly by rumors that new rifle cartridges are greased with cow and pig fat, and march to Delhi, where they proclaim the aging Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar their leader. The revolt spreads across northern and central India before British forces suppress it in 1858, with great brutality on both sides.
significance: Britain ended the East India Company's rule and the Mughal dynasty and governed India directly as the British Raj; in India the rebellion is often remembered as a first war of independence.

zh.title: 1857年印度起义
zh.summary: 东印度公司印度士兵在密拉特哗变，牛脂猪脂润滑子弹的传闻是诱因之一。他们进军德里，拥立末代莫卧儿皇帝，起义扩展至北部、中部，1858年被镇压，双方均犯下暴行。
zh.significance: 英国终结公司与莫卧儿统治，直接治理印度。印度常将其视为第一次独立战争。

title: British Raj
summary: After the rebellion of 1857 the British Crown took over the government of India from the East India Company. It ruled about two thirds of the subcontinent directly and the rest through princes, built railways and canals, and faced a growing nationalist movement.
significance: India was the centerpiece of the British Empire, and the end of the Raj in 1947 created India and Pakistan and began the wider end of European empires.

zh.title: 英属印度
zh.summary: 1857年起义后，英国王室接管印度，以直接统治及土邦间接统治治理次大陆，修建铁路、运河，并面对日益壮大的民族运动。
zh.significance: 印度是大英帝国核心，1947年殖民统治结束产生印度与巴基斯坦，也推动全球去殖民化。

title: Darwin's On the Origin of Species
summary: Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species, arguing that living things change over generations through natural selection, as individuals better suited to their environment survive and reproduce more. Drawing on his voyage on HMS Beagle and decades of research, he presents evidence that species descend from common ancestors. Alfred Russel Wallace had reached a similar idea independently, and their papers were presented together in 1858.
significance: Evolution by natural selection became the foundation of modern biology, and the book transformed debates about humanity's place in nature.

zh.title: 达尔文《物种起源》
zh.summary: 达尔文出版《物种起源》，论证生物通过自然选择逐代变化：更适应环境的个体留下更多后代。他以小猎犬号航行及数十年研究说明物种共有祖先。华莱士独立提出类似思想，两人的论文已于1858年共同发表。
zh.significance: 自然选择进化论成为现代生物学基础，也改变了人类如何理解自身在自然界中的地位。

title: American Civil War
summary: After Abraham Lincoln is elected president, eleven Southern slave states secede from the United States and form the Confederacy, and war, fought mainly over slavery and its expansion, begins when Confederate forces fire on Fort Sumter in April 1861. After four years of fighting, including the Battle of Gettysburg in 1863, the Union defeats the Confederacy in 1865.
significance: The war preserved the Union and led to the end of slavery in the United States with the Thirteenth Amendment, at a cost of an estimated 620,000 to 750,000 soldiers' lives.

zh.title: 美国南北战争
zh.summary: 林肯当选后，十一个南方蓄奴州脱离联邦，战争于1861年萨姆特堡遭炮击时爆发，主要围绕奴隶制及其扩张。1865年联邦取胜。
zh.significance: 战争维护国家统一，并通过第十三修正案废除奴隶制，代价为估计六十二万至七十五万军人死亡。

title: Empire of Japan
summary: After the Meiji Restoration, Japan was governed in the emperor's name under a constitution adopted in 1889. It industrialized rapidly, defeated China and Russia, and took Taiwan, Korea and Manchuria. In the 1930s the military took control and led the country into a war across Asia and the Pacific that ended in defeat in 1945.
significance: It was the first non-Western state to become a modern industrial and colonial power, and its expansion and defeat reshaped the whole of East Asia.

zh.title: 大日本帝国
zh.summary: 明治维新后，日本以天皇名义治理，1889年颁布宪法，迅速工业化并扩张至台湾、朝鲜和满洲。1930年代军方主导政治，将国家带入亚洲与太平洋战争，1945年战败。
zh.significance: 日本是首个成为现代工业及殖民强国的非西方国家，其扩张与败亡重塑整个东亚。

title: Meiji Japan
summary: The restoration of imperial government ended the Tokugawa regime and ushered in major administrative, military, educational, and industrial reforms. Japan developed into an imperial power during the Meiji emperor's reign.
significance: In a single generation Japan turned from a secluded feudal society into an industrial and military power, the first outside the West to do so.

zh.title: 日本明治时期
zh.summary: 恢复天皇名义上的统治终结德川幕府，开启行政、军事、教育与工业改革。明治天皇在位期间，日本发展为帝国强权。
zh.significance: 日本在一代人间由相对封闭的封建社会转为工业与军事强国，是西方以外最早完成这一转变的国家。

title: Meiji Restoration
summary: Samurai from domains such as Satsuma and Chōshū overthrow the Tokugawa shogunate and restore power in the name of the young Emperor Meiji, who moves his court to Edo, renamed Tokyo. The new leaders abolish the feudal domains and the privileges of the samurai and rapidly adopt Western-style industry, schooling, an army and, in 1889, a constitution.
significance: Within decades Japan became an industrial and military power, defeating China in 1895 and Russia in 1905 and building an empire in Asia.

zh.title: 明治维新
zh.summary: 萨摩、长州等藩的武士推翻德川幕府，以年轻的明治天皇名义恢复政权，迁都江户并改名东京。新政府废藩、取消武士特权，迅速采用西式工业、教育和军制，并于1889年颁布宪法。
zh.significance: 数十年内，日本成为工业与军事强国，1895年击败清朝、1905年击败俄国，并在亚洲建立殖民帝国。

title: Suez Canal opens
summary: After ten years of construction by a French-led company under Ferdinand de Lesseps, the Suez Canal opens across the isthmus of Suez in Egypt, linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. It is built largely by Egyptian laborers, many of them conscripted, and has no locks.
significance: By letting ships sail between Europe and Asia without going around Africa, the canal cut thousands of kilometers from the voyage between Britain and India and became one of the world's most important trade routes.

zh.title: 苏伊士运河开通
zh.summary: 由法国主导、费迪南·德·雷赛布领导的公司历时十年，在埃及苏伊士地峡建成连接地中海与红海的运河。主要劳力来自埃及，其中许多人遭强征。运河不设船闸。
zh.significance: 它使欧洲与亚洲间的船只无须绕行非洲，大幅缩短英国至印度航程，成为全球最重要的商路之一。

title: German Empire
summary: After Prussia's victory over France, the German states were united in 1871 under the Prussian king as emperor, with Bismarck as chancellor. Germany quickly became the strongest industrial and military power on the continent and acquired colonies in Africa and the Pacific. It collapsed in revolution at the end of World War I.
significance: A united Germany overturned the European balance of power, and the rivalries that followed led to World War I.

zh.title: 德意志帝国
zh.summary: 普鲁士击败法国后，1871年德意志诸邦在普王与宰相俾斯麦领导下统一，迅速成为欧洲大陆工业军事强国，并获得海外殖民地，一战末期在革命中瓦解。
zh.significance: 统一德国打破欧洲均势，随后强权竞争最终引向第一次世界大战。

title: Berlin Conference and the Scramble for Africa

location.name: Congo basin, near Kinshasa (representative; the conference met in Berlin)

summary: Representatives of fourteen states, mostly European, meet in Berlin at the invitation of the German chancellor Otto von Bismarck to agree rules for claiming African territory; no Africans are invited. Around the conference the powers recognize King Leopold II's personal claim to the Congo, and in the following decades European powers conquer and divide almost all of Africa, leaving only Ethiopia and Liberia independent by 1914.
significance: Colonial rule redrew Africa's map with borders that often ignored existing peoples and states, and most of those borders survive in today's African countries.

zh.title: 柏林会议与瓜分非洲
zh.summary: 俾斯麦邀请十四国代表在柏林讨论占领非洲的规则，无非洲人受邀。利奥波德二世对刚果的私人主张获认可，此后列强瓜分非洲，到1914年仅埃塞俄比亚与利比里亚独立。
zh.significance: 殖民边界往往无视原有民族与国家，其中大部分延续为今日非洲国界。
zh.locationName: 金沙萨附近刚果盆地（代表地点；会议于柏林召开）

title: Indian independence movement
summary: Organized nationalist politics, mass protest, civil disobedience, and other forms of resistance challenged British rule. This band begins with the founding of the Indian National Congress and ends with independence and partition; earlier resistance preceded it.
significance: It ended British rule over a fifth of humanity, and its methods of mass non-violent protest inspired later movements for independence and civil rights.

zh.title: 印度独立运动
zh.summary: 民族主义组织、群众抗议、不合作与其他抵抗方式挑战英国统治。此处以印度国民大会党成立至1947年独立分治为范围，更早已有反抗。
zh.significance: 运动结束对约世界五分之一人口的殖民统治，其大规模非暴力抗争影响后来的独立与民权运动。

title: French Indochina
summary: France conquered Vietnam in stages from 1858 and in 1887 joined it with Cambodia, and later Laos, in a single colonial federation run from Hanoi. It exported rice, rubber and coal for the benefit of French companies. After Japanese occupation in World War II, the Viet Minh fought the returning French and defeated them at Dien Bien Phu in 1954.
significance: The end of French rule left Vietnam divided, which led directly to the Vietnam War.

zh.title: 法属印度支那
zh.summary: 法国从1858年起逐步征服越南，1887年与柬埔寨、后来与老挝组成殖民联邦，输出稻米、橡胶与煤。二战后越盟抗击返回的法国军队，1954年在奠边府取胜。
zh.significance: 法属印度支那终结后越南分裂，直接通向后来的越南战争。

title: First Sino-Japanese War
summary: Japan and Qing China go to war over control of Korea. Japan's modernized army and navy win every major battle, destroying the Chinese fleet at Weihaiwei. By the Treaty of Shimonoseki, China recognizes Korea's independence, pays a large indemnity and cedes Taiwan to Japan.
significance: The war showed that Japan had overtaken China as the leading power in East Asia and set off a scramble by foreign powers for concessions in China.

zh.title: 甲午中日战争
zh.summary: 日本与清朝为争夺朝鲜控制权开战。日本近代化陆海军赢得主要战役，并在威海卫消灭北洋舰队。《马关条约》迫使清朝承认朝鲜独立、支付巨额赔款并割让台湾。
zh.significance: 战争表明日本已取代中国成为东亚领先强国，也引发列强争夺在华权益的浪潮。

title: Boxer Rebellion
summary: A peasant movement in northern China, known to foreigners as the Boxers, attacks Chinese Christians and missionaries, and with the support of the Qing court besieges the foreign legations in Beijing for 55 days in 1900. An army of eight nations relieves the siege, loots the capital and imposes a huge indemnity.
significance: The humiliation destroyed what remained of the Qing dynasty's standing and pushed it into late reforms, a decade before it fell.

zh.title: 义和团运动
zh.summary: 中国北方的义和团攻击中国基督徒与传教士，并获清廷支持，于1900年围攻北京外国使馆区55天。八国联军解围后洗劫首都，并迫使清朝支付巨额赔款。
zh.significance: 这次挫败进一步摧毁清廷威信，迫使其在覆亡前十年启动晚期改革。

title: Wright brothers' first powered flight

location.name: Kill Devil Hills, near Kitty Hawk

summary: Orville and Wilbur Wright, bicycle makers from Ohio, make the first widely recognized controlled, sustained flights in a powered, heavier-than-air airplane at Kill Devil Hills, near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. The first flight lasts 12 seconds and covers 37 meters, and the longest of the day's four flights about 59 seconds.
significance: Their way of controlling an aircraft in three dimensions laid the groundwork for modern aviation, which within decades transformed travel, trade and warfare.

zh.title: 莱特兄弟首次动力飞行
zh.summary: 来自俄亥俄州的自行车制造者奥维尔与威尔伯·莱特，在北卡罗来纳基蒂霍克附近实现广为承认的首次可控、持续、重于空气的动力飞行。首飞12秒、37米，当日最长一次约59秒。
zh.significance: 他们的三轴操纵方式奠定现代航空基础，随后数十年航空改变了旅行、贸易与战争。
zh.locationName: 基蒂霍克附近基尔代维尔山

title: Russo-Japanese War
summary: Japan and Russia fight over control of Manchuria and Korea. Japan opens with a surprise attack on the Russian fleet at Port Arthur, takes the fortress after a long siege, wins the land battle of Mukden and destroys a second Russian fleet in the Tsushima Strait in May 1905.
significance: It was the first victory of an Asian power over a European one in modern times; it gave Japan a free hand in Korea and shook the Russian monarchy.

zh.title: 日俄战争
zh.summary: 日本与俄国为争夺满洲和朝鲜的控制权开战。日本先突袭旅顺俄国舰队，长期围城后夺取要塞，继而赢得奉天会战，并于1905年5月在对马海峡歼灭另一支俄国舰队。
zh.significance: 这是近代亚洲强国战胜欧洲强国的重要转折，使日本得以进一步控制朝鲜，也动摇了俄国君主制。

title: Einstein's theory of relativity

location.name: Bern (where Einstein worked at the patent office)

summary: Albert Einstein, a 26-year-old clerk at the Swiss patent office in Bern, publishes four groundbreaking papers, including his special theory of relativity, which shows that measurements of time and space depend on the observer's motion, and the equation E = mc², linking mass and energy. In 1915 he extends it into the general theory of relativity, which explains gravity as the curving of space and time.
significance: Relativity overturned ideas about space and time that had stood since Newton, and it underlies modern physics and cosmology as well as technologies such as GPS.

zh.title: 爱因斯坦相对论
zh.summary: 在瑞士伯尔尼专利局任职的26岁爱因斯坦发表四篇突破性论文，包括狭义相对论与质能关系E=mc²。相对论指出，时空测量取决于观察者的运动。1915年，他又提出广义相对论，将引力解释为时空弯曲。
zh.significance: 相对论改变了牛顿以来的时空观，奠定现代物理学与宇宙学基础，也支撑GPS等技术。
zh.locationName: 伯尔尼（爱因斯坦任职专利局之地）

title: Korea under Japanese rule
summary: Japan annexed Korea in 1910 and ruled it as a colony for 35 years. It built railways and industry to serve its own empire, suppressed the Korean independence movement and, in the 1930s and 1940s, tried to erase Korean identity while conscripting Koreans for labor and war.
significance: The colonial period left deep wounds that still trouble relations between Korea and Japan, and it ended with the peninsula divided.

zh.title: 日本殖民统治下的朝鲜
zh.summary: 日本1910年吞并朝鲜，殖民统治35年，为帝国利益建设铁路和工业，镇压独立运动，并于1930、40年代强化同化，征发劳工与军人。
zh.significance: 殖民经历留下深刻创伤，持续影响朝日关系，结束时半岛又陷入分裂。

title: Xinhai Revolution ends imperial China
summary: An army uprising in Wuchang, in central China, sparks revolts across the provinces against the Qing dynasty. Revolutionaries proclaim the Republic of China with Sun Yat-sen as provisional president, and in February 1912 the six-year-old emperor Puyi abdicates.
significance: The revolution ended more than 2,000 years of imperial rule in China, but the new republic soon broke apart under warlords, opening decades of conflict.

zh.title: 辛亥革命终结中国帝制
zh.summary: 武昌的军队起义引发各省反清革命。革命者宣布建立中华民国，推举孙中山为临时大总统。1912年2月，六岁的溥仪退位。
zh.significance: 革命终结了中国两千余年的帝制，但新共和国很快陷入军阀割据，开启了数十年动荡。

title: Republic of China
summary: The republic that replaced the Qing dynasty soon broke up among rival warlords. The Nationalist Party under Chiang Kai-shek reunified much of the country from Nanjing in 1928, then faced Japanese invasion and a civil war with the Communists, which it lost.
significance: It ended more than two thousand years of imperial rule in China; after 1949 its government continued on Taiwan.

zh.title: 中华民国
zh.summary: 取代清朝的共和国很快陷入军阀割据。蒋介石领导的国民党1928年从南京统一大部分地区，继而面对日本入侵和国共内战，最终败于共产党。
zh.significance: 它终结中国两千余年帝制，1949年后政府继续在台湾运作。

title: World War I
summary: After a Bosnian Serb nationalist assassinates the Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, alliances draw the great powers into war, with Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire facing France, Russia, Britain and later Italy and the United States. Millions of soldiers die in the trench warfare of the Western Front and on other fronts, from machine guns, artillery and poison gas.
significance: Estimates of the dead, soldiers and civilians, range from about 15 to 22 million; the war destroyed the German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman empires, helped bring on the Russian Revolution and redrew the map of Europe and the Middle East.

zh.title: 第一次世界大战
zh.summary: 萨拉热窝刺杀事件引发联盟连锁反应，德、奥匈、奥斯曼与法、俄、英及后来的意、美交战。机枪、火炮、毒气与堑壕战造成巨大伤亡。
zh.significance: 军民死亡估计一千五百万至两千二百万，四大帝国瓦解，俄国革命发生，欧洲与中东版图重划。
zh.locationName: 凡尔登附近西线（代表地点）

title: Russian Revolution
summary: Strained by war, Russia erupts in revolution: in February (March in the Western calendar) strikes and mutinies in Petrograd force Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate, and a provisional government takes over. In October (November) the Bolsheviks under Vladimir Lenin seize power, and they win the civil war that follows by the early 1920s.
significance: The revolution created the first state ruled by a communist party, which became the Soviet Union, and its ideology and rivalry with the West shaped much of the 20th century.

zh.title: 俄国革命
zh.summary: 战争压力下，彼得格勒罢工与兵变迫使尼古拉二世在二月革命中退位。十月革命时，列宁领导布尔什维克夺权，并在20世纪20年代初赢得内战。两次革命在公历分别为3月和11月。
zh.significance: 革命建立首个共产党执政国家，后来组成苏联，其意识形态与西方竞争深刻影响20世纪。

title: March First Movement
summary: In Seoul, 33 religious and civic leaders sign a declaration of Korea's independence from Japan, and students read it aloud to a crowd. Peaceful demonstrations spread across the country and involve perhaps two million people before Japanese police and troops suppress them, killing thousands.
significance: The movement united Koreans behind independence and led to a provisional government in exile; South Korea marks 1 March as a national holiday.

zh.title: 三一运动
zh.summary: 首尔33位宗教与社会领袖签署朝鲜独立宣言，学生向人群宣读。和平示威扩展到全国，参加者可能达两百万人。日本军警随后镇压，造成数千人死亡。
zh.significance: 运动将民众团结于独立目标之下，并促成流亡临时政府。韩国将3月1日定为国定假日。

title: May Fourth Movement
summary: Students in Beijing march to protest the decision of the Paris Peace Conference to hand Germany's rights in Shandong province to Japan rather than back to China. Strikes and boycotts spread to other cities, and the government refuses to sign the treaty.
significance: The protests gave their name to a wider movement that rejected Confucian tradition in favor of science, democracy and writing in everyday language, and out of which the Chinese Communist Party grew.

zh.title: 五四运动
zh.summary: 巴黎和会决定把德国在山东的权益转交日本，而非归还中国，北京学生因此游行抗议。罢工和抵制运动扩展至其他城市，中国政府最终拒签和约。
zh.significance: 抗议与更广泛的思想文化运动相结合，推动科学、民主和白话文，挑战传统儒家秩序，也为中国共产党的兴起创造条件。

title: Chinese Communist Party founded
summary: Thirteen delegates, among them the young Mao Zedong, meet in secret in a house in Shanghai's French Concession, with two representatives of the Communist International, and found the Chinese Communist Party. They represent only about fifty members.
significance: Within three decades the party had won control of China, which it has governed ever since.

zh.title: 中国共产党成立
zh.summary: 包括青年毛泽东在内的十三位代表，与两位共产国际代表，在上海法租界一处住宅秘密开会，成立中国共产党。他们所代表的党员当时仅约五十人。
zh.significance: 不到三十年，该党便取得中国大陆的统治权，并一直执政至今。

title: Soviet Union
summary: The Soviet Union was a federation of republics ruled by the Communist Party from Moscow, formed after the Russian Revolution and civil war. Under Stalin it industrialized by force at enormous human cost; it bore the main burden of defeating Nazi Germany and then competed with the United States in the Cold War.
significance: It was the first communist state and one of two superpowers, and its collapse in 1991 ended the Cold War.

zh.title: 苏联
zh.summary: 苏联在俄国革命与内战后成立，由莫斯科的共产党治理。斯大林以巨大人命代价推进工业化，苏联承担击败纳粹德国的重要战争负担，战后与美国展开冷战。
zh.significance: 它是最早的共产主义国家和两大超级大国之一，1991年解体标志冷战结束。

title: Republic of Turkey
summary: After the Ottoman defeat in World War I, Mustafa Kemal, later called Ataturk, led a national movement that drove out the occupying armies and proclaimed a republic at Ankara in 1923. He abolished the sultanate and the caliphate, replaced Islamic law with European codes, adopted the Latin alphabet and gave women the vote.
significance: Turkey was the first Muslim-majority country to become a secular republic, a model that others debated for the rest of the century.

zh.title: 土耳其共和国
zh.summary: 奥斯曼一战战败后，穆斯塔法·凯末尔领导民族运动逐走占领军，1923年在安卡拉建立共和国，废除苏丹与哈里发制度，采用世俗法律、拉丁字母并给予女性选举权。
zh.significance: 土耳其成为穆斯林占多数国家中早期的世俗共和国，其模式在此后长期受到讨论。

title: Pahlavi Iran
summary: Reza Khan, an army officer, deposed the last Qajar shah and took the throne in 1925. He and his son Mohammad Reza used oil revenue to build a modern army, industry and schools while ruling as autocrats, the son with strong American backing after a coup in 1953. The revolution of 1979 ended the monarchy.
significance: Rapid modernization from above without political freedom produced the Islamic Revolution, which reshaped the politics of the Middle East.

zh.title: 伊朗巴列维王朝
zh.summary: 军官礼萨汗1925年废黜卡扎尔末王。他与儿子穆罕默德·礼萨以石油收入推动军队、工业和教育现代化，同时实行专制；1953年政变后，后者更获美国支持。1979年革命终结王朝。
zh.significance: 缺乏政治自由的自上而下现代化激化矛盾，最终引向改变中东政治的伊斯兰革命。

title: Chinese Civil War
summary: Nationalist and Communist forces fought intermittently for control of China, with a major interruption during the war against Japan. Communist victory on the mainland led to the People's Republic of China, while the Nationalist government withdrew to Taiwan; later confrontations continued.
significance: The Communist victory created the People's Republic of China and left Taiwan under a separate government, a division that persists.

zh.title: 国共内战
zh.summary: 国民党与共产党间歇争夺中国政权，抗日战争期间主要战事中断。共产党在大陆获胜后建立中华人民共和国，国民政府撤往台湾，双方对峙继续。
zh.significance: 内战结局形成中华人民共和国与台湾分治的格局，影响延续至今。

title: Discovery of penicillin
summary: At St Mary's Hospital in London, the Scottish bacteriologist Alexander Fleming notices that a mold, Penicillium, has killed the bacteria around it in a culture dish. He names the substance it produces penicillin, but only in the early 1940s do Howard Florey, Ernst Chain and their team at Oxford purify it and show that it can cure infections.
significance: Mass-produced from World War II onward, penicillin became one of the first widely used antibiotics, opening an era in which many once-deadly infections could be cured and saving many millions of lives.

zh.title: 青霉素的发现
zh.summary: 伦敦圣玛丽医院的苏格兰细菌学家亚历山大·弗莱明发现，培养皿中的青霉菌杀死了周围细菌，并将其产生的物质命名为青霉素。直到20世纪40年代初，弗洛里、钱恩及牛津团队才将其提纯并证明能够治疗感染。
zh.significance: 二战期间及之后的大规模生产，使青霉素成为最早广泛使用的抗生素之一，挽救了数百万生命。

title: Great Depression begins
summary: Share prices on the New York Stock Exchange crash, wiping out fortunes and shaking confidence. Bank failures, falling trade and collapsing prices follow, and by 1933 about a quarter of the US workforce is unemployed as the slump spreads around the world. Economists still debate how much the crash itself caused the depression that followed.
significance: The Depression lasted through much of the 1930s, led governments to take a larger role in managing economies, and fed the rise of extremist movements such as Nazism in Germany.

zh.title: 经济大萧条开始
zh.summary: 纽约股市暴跌后，银行倒闭、贸易萎缩与价格下跌相继发生，1933年美国约四分之一劳动力失业，危机蔓延全球。股灾在其中的因果作用仍有经济学争论。
zh.significance: 萧条持续1930年代大部，促使政府加强经济管理，也为德国纳粹等极端运动兴起创造条件。

title: Mukden Incident
summary: Officers of the Japanese army stationed in Manchuria blow up a short stretch of a Japanese-owned railway near Mukden, blame Chinese troops, and use the incident as a pretext to occupy the whole of Manchuria. Tokyo's civilian government fails to rein them in.
significance: It began fourteen years of Japanese aggression in China, showed that the League of Nations could not stop a determined aggressor, and put the Japanese army beyond civilian control.

zh.title: 九一八事变
zh.summary: 驻满洲日军军官炸毁沈阳附近一小段日本控制的铁路，嫁祸中国军队，并以此为借口占领整个满洲。东京文官政府未能约束军方。
zh.significance: 事变开启日本长达十四年的侵华战争，暴露国际联盟阻止侵略的无力，也使日本军队进一步摆脱文官控制。

title: Manchukuo
summary: After seizing Manchuria, Japan set up a state there with Puyi, the last emperor of China, as its nominal ruler. Real power lay with the Japanese army, which developed the region's heavy industry for its own war effort. The state collapsed when the Soviet Union invaded in August 1945.
significance: Manchukuo was the model of a puppet state, recognized by few countries, and Japan's refusal to give it up led to its withdrawal from the League of Nations.

zh.title: 伪满洲国
zh.summary: 日本占领满洲后，扶植末代皇帝溥仪为名义统治者，实权掌握在日军手中，重工业服务于日本战争。1945年8月苏军进攻后，政权崩溃。
zh.significance: 它是少数国家承认的典型傀儡政权，日本拒绝放弃控制，最终退出国际联盟。

title: Nazi Germany
summary: Adolf Hitler became chancellor in 1933 and within months turned Germany into a one-party dictatorship. The regime rearmed, annexed Austria and Czechoslovakia, and began World War II by invading Poland in 1939. It murdered about six million Jews in the Holocaust, and millions of others, before its total defeat in 1945.
significance: Nazi Germany caused the most destructive war in history and committed genocide on an industrial scale; the postwar order was built to prevent a repetition.

zh.title: 纳粹德国
zh.summary: 希特勒1933年任总理后迅速建立一党独裁，扩军、吞并领土，1939年入侵波兰发动世界大战。政权在大屠杀中杀害约六百万犹太人及数百万其他受害者，1945年战败。
zh.significance: 纳粹德国造成史上最惨烈的战争，并实施工业化规模的种族灭绝，战后秩序旨在防止重演。

title: Long March

location.name: Zunyi (where Mao rose to leadership on the march)

summary: Surrounded by Nationalist armies in the southeast, the Chinese Communists break out and retreat for a year across some of the roughest country in China, covering thousands of kilometers before reaching Shaanxi in the northwest. Of about 86,000 who set out with the main force, fewer than one in ten arrive.
significance: The march saved the Communist movement from destruction, made Mao Zedong its leader, and became the founding legend of the People's Republic.

zh.title: 长征
zh.summary: 中国共产党军队在东南部遭国民党军包围后突围，历时一年，穿越险峻地区，行军数千公里抵达西北陕西。主力出发时约八万六千人，到达者不足十分之一。
zh.significance: 长征使共产党免于覆灭，确立毛泽东的领导地位，并成为中华人民共和国建国叙事的重要部分。
zh.locationName: 遵义（长征中毛泽东确立领导地位之地）

title: Nanjing Massacre
summary: After capturing Nanjing, then China's capital, Japanese troops spend about six weeks killing prisoners of war and civilians and raping women on a mass scale. Estimates of the dead range from tens of thousands to more than 300,000; a postwar tribunal put the number at over 200,000.
significance: It is the most notorious atrocity of the war in Asia, and disputes over how it is remembered still strain relations between China and Japan.

zh.title: 南京大屠杀
zh.summary: 日军攻占当时中国首都南京后，在约六周内大规模杀害战俘和平民，并强奸妇女。遇难人数估计从数万到三十余万不等，战后法庭认定超过二十万。
zh.significance: 这是亚洲战场最恶名昭彰的暴行之一，围绕其历史记忆的争议至今仍影响中日关系。

title: Second Sino-Japanese War

location.name: Marco Polo Bridge, near Beijing (where the war began)

summary: A clash between Chinese and Japanese troops near Beijing in July 1937 grows into a full invasion. Japan takes the coast, the great cities and the railways, but China's government retreats inland to Chongqing and fights on for eight years, tying down more than a million Japanese soldiers. From 1941 the war is part of World War II.
significance: It was the largest Asian war of the 20th century, with Chinese deaths estimated at 15 to 20 million; it left the Nationalist government exhausted and helped the Communists win the civil war.

zh.title: 全面抗日战争
zh.summary: 1937年7月北京附近的中日军队冲突扩大为全面战争。日本占领沿海、大城市与铁路，中国政府却内迁重庆，坚持抗战八年，牵制超过百万日军。1941年起，这场战争成为第二次世界大战的一部分。
zh.significance: 这是20世纪亚洲规模最大的战争，中国死亡人数估计为一千五百万至两千万。战争耗尽国民政府力量，也有利于共产党后来赢得内战。
zh.locationName: 北京附近卢沟桥（战争爆发地）

title: World War II
summary: Germany under Adolf Hitler invades Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France declare war; in Asia, Japan has been at war with China since 1937. The war spreads worldwide, with the Allies, led by Britain, the Soviet Union, the United States and China, fighting the Axis powers of Germany, Italy and Japan, until Germany surrenders in May 1945 and Japan in August.
significance: The deadliest conflict in history, it killed an estimated 70 to 85 million people, including about six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust, and left the United States and the Soviet Union as rival superpowers.

zh.title: 第二次世界大战
zh.summary: 1939年9月德国入侵波兰，英法宣战；亚洲的中日战争已持续两年。英、苏、美、中等同盟国与德、意、日轴心国全球交战，至1945年德日投降。
zh.significance: 战争造成约七千万至八千五百万人死亡，包括大屠杀中约六百万犹太人，是史上最致命冲突，战后美苏成为对立超级大国。
zh.locationName: 华沙（1939年德国入侵波兰，代表地点）

title: Korea divided at the 38th parallel
summary: As Japan surrenders, the United States proposes and the Soviet Union accepts a line along the 38th parallel to divide their zones of occupation in Korea. Meant to be temporary, the division hardens as the Cold War sets in, and in 1948 separate governments are proclaimed in Seoul and Pyongyang.
significance: The line became the border between two hostile states, led to the Korean War, and still divides the peninsula.

zh.title: 朝鲜半岛沿三八线分裂
zh.summary: 日本投降时，美国提出、苏联接受以北纬38度划分朝鲜占领区。原拟临时的安排随着冷战固定下来，1948年首尔与平壤分别成立政府。
zh.significance: 分区演变为敌对国家边界，引发朝鲜战争，半岛分裂至今仍未结束。

title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
summary: The United States drops atomic bombs on the Japanese cities of Hiroshima on 6 August and Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, the only use of nuclear weapons in war to date. The bombs kill an estimated 150,000 to 246,000 people by the end of the year, most of them civilians, many from burns and radiation sickness.
significance: Japan announced its surrender days later, after the Soviet Union had also declared war on it, and the bombings opened the nuclear age; historians still debate whether they were necessary to end the war.

zh.title: 广岛与长崎原子弹轰炸
zh.summary: 美国于1945年8月6日、9日分别向广岛和长崎投下原子弹。到年底估计十五万至二十四万六千人死亡，多为平民，许多人死于烧伤和辐射。
zh.significance: 苏联也对日宣战后，日本数日内宣布投降。轰炸开启核时代，其是否为结束战争所必需，至今仍有历史争论。

title: Indonesia declares independence
summary: Two days after Japan's surrender ends its wartime occupation of the Dutch East Indies, the nationalist leaders Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta proclaim Indonesia's independence in Jakarta. The Dutch try to restore colonial rule, and four years of war and negotiation follow until the Netherlands transfers sovereignty in December 1949.
significance: Indonesia, a nation of thousands of islands and hundreds of ethnic groups, became one of the world's most populous countries and the most populous Muslim-majority nation.

zh.title: 印度尼西亚宣布独立
zh.summary: 日本投降两天后，苏加诺与哈达在雅加达宣布印尼独立。荷兰试图恢复殖民统治，随后四年战争与谈判，至1949年12月移交主权。
zh.significance: 由数千岛屿和数百族群组成的印尼，成为世界人口最多的国家之一，也是人口最多的穆斯林占多数国家。

title: United Nations founded

location.name: San Francisco (where the UN Charter was signed)

summary: Delegates of 50 countries meeting in San Francisco sign the Charter of the United Nations in June 1945, and the organization formally comes into being on 24 October. It aims to prevent future wars, with a Security Council in which five major powers (the United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France and China) hold permanent seats and a veto.
significance: With nearly every country now a member, the UN became the main forum for international diplomacy, peacekeeping and humanitarian work, though rivalry among the great powers often limits what it can do.

zh.title: 联合国成立
zh.summary: 五十国代表1945年6月在旧金山签署《联合国宪章》，组织于10月24日成立。安理会由美、苏、英、法、中五国拥有常任席位和否决权，以维护国际和平。
zh.significance: 联合国成为主要的国际外交、维和与人道工作平台，但大国竞争常限制其行动。
zh.locationName: 旧金山（《联合国宪章》签署地）

title: Cold War
summary: The United States, Soviet Union, and their allies competed through military alliances, nuclear deterrence, political confrontation, and proxy wars. Although placed in the Europe lane, the rivalry shaped events across the world.
significance: It divided the world into rival blocs for more than forty years, drove the nuclear arms race and the space race, and shaped the politics of nearly every country.

zh.title: 冷战
zh.summary: 美国、苏联及盟友通过军事联盟、核威慑、政治对抗与代理人战争竞争。虽在时间轴列于欧洲，其影响遍及全球。
zh.significance: 冷战将世界分成对立阵营四十余年，推动核军备与太空竞赛，塑造几乎所有国家的政治。

title: Republic of India
summary: India became independent in 1947 with Jawaharlal Nehru as prime minister and adopted a constitution in 1950 as a secular, federal republic with universal suffrage. It kept a planned economy and stayed non-aligned in the Cold War, fought wars with Pakistan and China, and began opening its economy in 1991.
significance: India has remained the world's largest democracy, in a country of great poverty and diversity where many expected democracy to fail.

zh.title: 印度共和国
zh.summary: 印度1947年独立，尼赫鲁任总理，1950年确立世俗联邦共和国与普选制度。它实行计划经济、冷战不结盟政策，经历对巴基斯坦和中国的战争，1991年启动经济开放。
zh.significance: 印度在贫困与高度多样化的社会中维持世界最大规模的民主制度。

title: Independence and Partition of India
summary: British rule over India ends with the subcontinent divided into two independent states: India, with a Hindu majority, and Pakistan, with a Muslim majority, in two parts in the west and east. Hastily drawn borders through Punjab and Bengal set off mass violence and one of the largest migrations in history, as an estimated 10 to 20 million people cross them. Estimates of the dead range from about 200,000 to two million.
significance: India became the world's largest democracy, while Partition left a lasting hostility between India and Pakistan, including the unresolved dispute over Kashmir.

zh.title: 印度独立与印巴分治
zh.summary: 英国统治结束，次大陆分为印度教人口占多数的印度及东西两部分组成的穆斯林国家巴基斯坦。仓促划界引发暴力，一千万至两千万人迁移，死亡估计二十万至两百万。
zh.significance: 印度成为最大民主国家，但分治留下印巴长期敌对与克什米尔争议。

title: Pakistan
summary: Pakistan was created in 1947 as a homeland for the Muslims of British India, in two parts separated by 1,600 kilometers of Indian territory. The eastern part broke away as Bangladesh in 1971 after a war. Its politics alternated between elected governments and military rule, and it tested nuclear weapons in 1998.
significance: Its rivalry with India, centered on Kashmir, has been one of the world's most dangerous disputes, and both states are now nuclear powers.

zh.title: 巴基斯坦
zh.summary: 巴基斯坦1947年作为英属印度穆斯林家园成立，东西两部分相隔一千六百公里。东部在1971年战争后独立为孟加拉国，政治此后在民选与军政间交替，1998年进行核试验。
zh.significance: 围绕克什米尔的印巴争端长期危险，两国成为核国家后更具全球影响。

title: Postwar Japan
summary: Under American occupation Japan adopted a new constitution in 1947 that made the emperor a symbol, gave power to an elected parliament and renounced war. Independent again from 1952 and allied with the United States, it rebuilt its industry and by 1968 had the second-largest economy in the world.
significance: Japan's recovery from total defeat to prosperity as a peaceful democracy was a model for the rest of East Asia.

zh.title: 战后日本
zh.summary: 美国占领下，日本1947年实施新宪法，天皇成为象征，议会掌握政治权力，并放弃战争。1952年恢复独立后与美国结盟，重建工业，1968年成为世界第二大经济体。
zh.significance: 日本从全面战败转为繁荣的和平民主国家，为东亚其他地区提供发展范例。

title: State of Israel
summary: As British rule in Palestine ended, David Ben-Gurion declared the State of Israel on 14 May 1948, following a United Nations plan to partition the land. Neighboring Arab states invaded the next day; Israel survived, and some 700,000 Palestinian Arabs fled or were expelled. Further wars followed in 1956, 1967 and 1973, and peace with Egypt in 1979.
significance: Israel gave the Jewish people a state after the Holocaust, and the unresolved conflict with the Palestinians has shaped the Middle East ever since.

zh.title: 以色列国
zh.summary: 英国在巴勒斯坦统治结束时，本-古里安于1948年5月14日宣布建国，邻国翌日入侵。以色列存续下来，约七十万巴勒斯坦阿拉伯人逃离或被驱逐；后来又经历数次战争，1979年与埃及议和。
zh.significance: 以色列使犹太人在大屠杀后拥有国家，但与巴勒斯坦人的未决冲突持续塑造中东。

title: North Korea
summary: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea was founded in the Soviet zone of occupation under Kim Il Sung, who invaded the South in 1950. After the war he built a closed, heavily armed state around his own rule and passed power to his son Kim Jong Il in 1994, as the loss of Soviet aid and a famine devastated the country.
significance: It is the world's most isolated state and the only communist one to become a hereditary dynasty.

zh.title: 朝鲜
zh.summary: 金日成在苏联占领区建立朝鲜民主主义人民共和国，1950年进攻南方。战后形成封闭、高度军事化的国家，1994年传位金正日，其时苏援消失与饥荒重创社会。
zh.significance: 朝鲜成为高度孤立、由同一家族世袭领导的共产主义国家。

title: South Korea
summary: The Republic of Korea was founded in the American zone of occupation and was left among the poorest countries in the world by the Korean War. Under military-backed governments from 1961 it industrialized at great speed through export manufacturing, and after mass protests in 1987 it became a democracy.
significance: Its rise from poverty to wealth and democracy within two generations is one of the most striking transformations of the 20th century.

zh.title: 韩国
zh.summary: 大韩民国成立于美国占领区，朝鲜战争后极度贫困。1961年起，在军方支持的政府下依靠出口制造业迅速工业化，1987年群众抗议后转向民主。
zh.significance: 从贫困到富裕与民主的两代人转变，是20世纪最显著的社会变迁之一。

title: People's Republic of China founded
summary: As the Communists win the civil war against Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists, whose government retreats to Taiwan by the end of the year, Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China from Tiananmen Gate in Beijing. The Chinese Communist Party takes control of mainland China.
significance: Communist rule unified China under a strong central state, and after the upheavals of the Mao years it became, from the 1980s, one of the world's fastest-growing economies and a major global power.

zh.title: 中华人民共和国成立
zh.summary: 共产党在内战中战胜国民党，毛泽东在北京天安门宣布中华人民共和国成立。国民政府于年底前撤往台湾，共产党控制中国大陆。
zh.significance: 新的中央政权统一大陆，经历毛时代动荡后，自1980年代起中国成为增长最快的经济体之一和重要世界强国。

title: People's Republic of China
summary: The People's Republic was proclaimed in 1949 after the Communist victory in the civil war. Under Mao Zedong it collectivized the economy and went through the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution; reforms begun under Deng Xiaoping in 1978 opened it to markets and trade.
significance: It united mainland China under one government and, after the reforms, grew into one of the world's largest economies and a major global power.

zh.title: 中华人民共和国
zh.summary: 共产党内战获胜后，1949年建立中华人民共和国。毛泽东时期推行经济集体化，经历大跃进与文化大革命；1978年邓小平推动改革，逐渐引入市场与对外贸易。
zh.significance: 大陆在同一政府下统一，改革后发展为世界最大经济体之一与主要全球力量。

title: Taiwan (Republic of China)
summary: After losing the civil war, Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist government moved to Taiwan with about two million soldiers and refugees and ruled under martial law until 1987. The island industrialized rapidly, lost China's seat at the United Nations to Beijing in 1971, and held its first direct presidential election in 1996.
significance: Taiwan became a prosperous democracy whose status remains one of the most dangerous unresolved disputes in world politics.

zh.title: 台湾（中华民国）
zh.summary: 国民党内战失败后，蒋介石政府与约两百万军民迁往台湾，戒严延续至1987年。台湾快速工业化，1971年失去联合国中国代表席位，1996年举行首次总统直选。
zh.significance: 台湾发展为繁荣民主社会，其政治地位仍是国际政治中危险且未解决的争议之一。

title: Korean War
summary: War between North and South Korea drew in United Nations forces, led by the United States, and China. The 1953 armistice ended major fighting but left the peninsula divided without a peace treaty.
significance: It fixed the division of Korea into two hostile states and turned the Cold War into a global military confrontation.

zh.title: 朝鲜战争
zh.summary: 朝鲜半岛南北战争引入美国主导的联合国军与中国。1953年停战协定结束大规模战斗，却没有和平条约，半岛仍分裂。
zh.significance: 战争固定了南北敌对格局，也将冷战扩大为全球军事对抗。

title: Structure of DNA discovered
summary: At the University of Cambridge, James Watson and Francis Crick propose that DNA is a double helix: two strands wound around each other and joined by pairs of chemical bases. Their model relies heavily on X-ray images and data from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins at King's College London, notably an image from Franklin's lab known as Photo 51.
significance: The structure showed how genetic information is stored and copied, opening the way to molecular biology, genetic engineering and DNA sequencing.

zh.title: DNA双螺旋结构的发现
zh.summary: 剑桥的沃森与克里克提出DNA双螺旋模型：两条链相互盘绕，碱基配对连接。他们高度依赖伦敦国王学院富兰克林与威尔金斯的X射线数据，尤其是富兰克林实验室拍摄的“照片51”。
zh.significance: 这一结构揭示了遗传信息的储存与复制机制，开启了分子生物学、基因工程与DNA测序的发展。

title: Japanese economic miracle
summary: For nearly two decades Japan's economy grew by about ten percent a year. Close cooperation between government and business, high savings, new technology and exports of steel, ships, cars and electronics made it the second-largest economy in the world by 1968. The oil shock of 1973 brought the fastest growth to an end.
significance: Japan's export-led growth was the model later followed by South Korea, Taiwan and China.

zh.title: 日本经济奇迹
zh.summary: 近二十年间，日本经济年均增长约百分之十。政企合作、高储蓄、新技术和出口推动发展，1968年成为世界第二大经济体，1973年石油危机终结最快增长阶段。
zh.significance: 日本出口导向模式后来为韩国、台湾与中国借鉴。

title: Vietnam War
summary: After the French defeat in 1954, Vietnam is divided into a communist North and a US-backed South, and communist-led insurgents, supported by the North, fight the southern government. From 1965 the United States sends hundreds of thousands of troops, while the Soviet Union and China supply the North. US forces withdraw in 1973, and North Vietnamese forces take Saigon in April 1975, reuniting the country.
significance: Estimates of the dead range from about one million to over three million, most of them Vietnamese, along with more than 58,000 Americans; the war also spread into Laos and Cambodia and deeply divided American society.

zh.title: 越南战争
zh.summary: 法国退出后，越南分为共产主义北方与美国支持的南方。1965年起美国投入数十万军队，苏中援助北方。美军1973年撤出，北越1975年攻占西贡，完成统一。
zh.significance: 死亡估计一百万至三百余万，多为越南人，另有五万八千余美国人；战争波及老挝、柬埔寨，也撕裂美国社会。

title: Ghana's independence leads African decolonization
summary: The British colony of the Gold Coast becomes independent as Ghana, led by Kwame Nkrumah, after a decade of nationalist campaigning. It is one of the first colonies in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence, following Sudan in 1956.
significance: Ghana's independence inspired anti-colonial movements across the continent, and by the late 1960s most of Africa's former colonies had become independent states.

zh.title: 加纳独立推动非洲去殖民化
zh.summary: 经过十年民族主义运动，英属黄金海岸在恩克鲁玛领导下以加纳之名独立，成为继1956年苏丹之后较早独立的撒哈拉以南殖民地之一。
zh.significance: 加纳鼓舞全非洲反殖民运动，到20世纪60年代末，多数前殖民地已经独立。

title: Sputnik, the first satellite
summary: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1, a 58-centimeter metal ball with four long antennas, from a launch site in what is now Kazakhstan, putting the first artificial satellite into orbit around the Earth. Its radio beeps can be picked up by listeners around the world.
significance: Sputnik shocked the United States and started the space race, leading to the creation of NASA, heavy investment in science education and, in 1969, the Moon landing.

zh.title: 斯普特尼克一号：首颗人造卫星
zh.summary: 苏联从今哈萨克斯坦的发射场将斯普特尼克一号送入地球轨道，成为首颗人造卫星。它是直径58厘米、带四根长天线的金属球，全球听众都可接收其无线电信号。
zh.significance: 发射震动美国，开启太空竞赛，推动美国航天局成立、科学教育投资及1969年登月。

title: Great Leap Forward

location.name: Beijing (representative; the famine was worst in inland provinces)

summary: Mao Zedong launches a campaign to overtake the industrial powers within years. Farmers are organized into huge communes and millions are set to making steel in backyard furnaces, while officials report harvests that do not exist and the state takes grain on that basis. The result is the deadliest famine in recorded history.
significance: Estimates of the deaths range from about 15 million to 45 million or more; the disaster weakened Mao's position and led him to launch the Cultural Revolution to regain it.

zh.title: 大跃进
zh.summary: 毛泽东发起运动，试图在数年内赶超工业强国。农民被组织进大型人民公社，数百万人参与土法炼钢；官员虚报粮食产量，国家据此征粮，最终导致有史以来最严重的饥荒。
zh.significance: 死亡人数估计约为一千五百万至四千五百万或更多。灾难削弱了毛泽东的地位，并成为他后来发动文化大革命、重掌权力的背景。
zh.locationName: 北京（代表地点；内陆省份饥荒最为严重）

title: Cuban Missile Crisis

location.name: Havana (representative; the missile sites were across western Cuba)

summary: US spy planes discover that the Soviet Union is secretly installing nuclear missiles in Cuba, about 150 km from Florida, and President John F. Kennedy orders a naval blockade, called a quarantine, of the island. For thirteen days the world faces the risk of nuclear war, until Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev agrees to remove the missiles in return for a US pledge not to invade Cuba and a secret promise to withdraw US missiles from Turkey.
significance: It is often seen as the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war, and afterward the superpowers set up a direct hotline and signed a treaty limiting nuclear tests.

zh.title: 古巴导弹危机
zh.summary: 美国发现苏联在古巴部署核导弹，肯尼迪下令海上封锁。十三天核战危机后，赫鲁晓夫同意撤弹，换取美国不入侵古巴及秘密撤除土耳其导弹的承诺。
zh.significance: 这是冷战最接近核战争的时刻之一，随后双方建立热线，并签署限制核试验的条约。
zh.locationName: 哈瓦那（代表地点；导弹阵地遍布古巴西部）

title: First bullet train
summary: Japan opens the Tokaido Shinkansen between Tokyo and Osaka, with trains running at up to 210 kilometers an hour on a dedicated line. It opens nine days before the Tokyo Olympics, the first held in Asia.
significance: It was the world's first high-speed railway and, with the Olympics, announced Japan's return as an advanced nation.

zh.title: 首条新干线开通
zh.summary: 东京至大阪的东海道新干线开通，专线列车最高时速210公里，比东京奥运会开幕早九天。
zh.significance: 世界首条高速铁路与亚洲首届奥运会一同，象征日本重返先进国家行列。

title: Cultural Revolution
summary: Mao Zedong launches the Cultural Revolution to purge rivals and what he calls bourgeois and traditional elements from Chinese society. Young Red Guards attack teachers, officials and intellectuals and destroy temples and historical relics, and millions of urban youths are later sent to the countryside; the movement ends with Mao's death in 1976.
significance: Estimates of the dead range from hundreds of thousands to about two million or more, and the chaos discredited radical Maoism and helped open the way for Deng Xiaoping's reforms.

zh.title: 文化大革命
zh.summary: 毛泽东发动文化大革命，清除政治对手及其所称的资产阶级与传统因素。红卫兵攻击教师、官员和知识分子，破坏寺庙与文物，随后数百万城市青年被送往农村。运动在1976年毛泽东去世后结束。
zh.significance: 死亡人数估计从数十万到约两百万或更多。动乱削弱了激进毛主义的声望，也为邓小平改革创造了条件。

title: Apollo 11 Moon landing
summary: NASA's Apollo 11 mission lands Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon while Michael Collins orbits above. The two astronauts spend about two and a half hours walking on the lunar surface before returning safely to Earth.
significance: It was the first time humans set foot on another world, and the high point of the Cold War space race between the United States and the Soviet Union.

zh.title: 阿波罗11号登月
zh.summary: 阿波罗11号将阿姆斯特朗与奥尔德林送上月球，柯林斯留在月球轨道。两人在月面活动约两个半小时，随后安全返回地球。
zh.significance: 这是人类首次踏上地球以外的天体，也是美苏太空竞赛的高潮。

title: Nixon visits China
summary: Richard Nixon becomes the first American president to visit the People's Republic of China, meeting Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai after more than twenty years in which the two countries had no relations. In a joint statement issued in Shanghai, both sides agree to work toward normal relations and set out their differences over Taiwan.
significance: The opening shifted the balance of the Cold War against the Soviet Union and prepared the way for China's later entry into the world economy.

zh.title: 尼克松访华
zh.summary: 中美断绝正常往来二十余年后，尼克松成为首位访问中华人民共和国的美国总统，会见毛泽东与周恩来。双方在上海发表联合公报，同意推动关系正常化，并陈述各自在台湾问题上的立场。
zh.significance: 这次接触改变了冷战力量格局，对苏联形成压力，也为中国后来融入世界经济铺路。

title: Deng Xiaoping's economic reforms
summary: Two years after Mao's death, Deng Xiaoping becomes China's leading figure and, at a Communist Party meeting in December 1978, launches a policy of 'reform and opening up'. Farmers are allowed to sell surplus crops for profit, private businesses are gradually permitted, and special economic zones such as Shenzhen open to foreign investment.
significance: The reforms began decades of very rapid growth that lifted hundreds of millions of people out of poverty and made China a leading industrial and trading power, while the Communist Party kept its monopoly on political power.

zh.title: 邓小平推动经济改革
zh.summary: 毛泽东去世两年后，邓小平成为中国主要领导人，并于1978年12月的中共会议上推动改革开放。农民逐渐获准出售剩余农产品获利，私营经济逐步获准发展，深圳等经济特区向外资开放。
zh.significance: 改革开启了数十年的高速增长，使数亿人脱离贫困，中国成为工业与贸易大国；共产党同时继续掌握政治权力。
zh.locationName: 深圳（经济特区，代表地点）

title: Iranian Revolution
summary: After a year of mass protests and strikes against Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, the shah leaves Iran and the exiled cleric Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini returns to a huge welcome. His supporters take power, and a referendum makes Iran an Islamic Republic, with Khomeini as Supreme Leader.
significance: The revolution created a state ruled by Shia clergy, turned Iran from a US ally into an opponent, and inspired Islamist political movements across the Muslim world.

zh.title: 伊朗革命
zh.summary: 针对穆罕默德·礼萨·巴列维国王的大规模抗议和罢工持续一年后，国王离境，流亡教士霍梅尼返回并受到热烈欢迎。其支持者掌权，经公投建立伊斯兰共和国，霍梅尼任最高领袖。
zh.significance: 革命建立了什叶派教士主导的国家，使伊朗从美国盟友转为对手，并激发各地伊斯兰政治运动。

title: South Korea's June Democratic Struggle
summary: After a student dies under police torture and the military-backed president names his successor, millions of South Koreans take to the streets for nearly three weeks. On 29 June the government gives way and accepts direct presidential elections and the restoration of civil rights.
significance: The protests ended decades of authoritarian rule; South Korea has been a democracy since.

zh.title: 韩国六月民主运动
zh.summary: 一名学生遭警察刑讯致死，军方支持的总统又指定继承人，数百万韩国人因此连续近三周上街。6月29日，政府接受总统直选与恢复公民权利。
zh.significance: 抗议终结数十年威权统治，韩国此后进入民主时代。

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
summary: As protests and mass emigration shake communist East Germany, its government announces that citizens may cross the border, and crowds pour through the checkpoints of the Berlin Wall, which has divided the city since 1961. Germans from both sides climb on the wall and begin chipping it apart.
significance: The fall of the wall became the symbol of the end of communist rule in Eastern Europe and of the Cold War division of Europe, and Germany was reunified in October 1990.

zh.title: 柏林墙倒塌
zh.summary: 抗议与外逃浪潮动摇东德后，政府宣布公民可越境。人群涌过自1961年分隔城市的柏林墙检查站，东西两侧居民登墙并开始拆除。
zh.significance: 柏林墙倒塌成为东欧共产主义统治与欧洲冷战分裂结束的象征，德国于1990年10月统一。

title: Tiananmen Square protests
summary: Students occupying Tiananmen Square in Beijing to call for political reform and an end to corruption are joined by workers and residents, and protests spread to other cities. On the night of 3 to 4 June the army clears the streets around the square with tanks and gunfire. Estimates of the dead range from several hundred to several thousand.
significance: The crackdown ended hopes of political liberalization alongside China's economic reforms, and discussion of it remains censored in China.

zh.title: 天安门广场抗议
zh.summary: 北京学生占据天安门广场，要求政治改革、反对腐败，工人与市民随后加入，抗议也扩展到其他城市。6月3日至4日夜间，军队以坦克与枪火清理广场周边街道。死亡人数估计从数百到数千不等。
zh.significance: 镇压终结了经济改革伴随政治自由化的期待，对这一事件的讨论在中国仍受到审查。

title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
summary: After a failed coup by communist hardliners in August 1991, the Soviet republics declare independence one after another. Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president on 25 December, and the Soviet Union is formally dissolved the next day, splitting into fifteen independent countries, the largest of them Russia.
significance: It marked the end of the Cold War and left the United States as the sole superpower, while the former Soviet states went through hard economic and political transitions.

zh.title: 苏联解体
zh.summary: 1991年8月强硬派政变失败后，各加盟共和国相继独立。戈尔巴乔夫12月25日辞职，翌日苏联正式解体，分为十五国，其中俄罗斯最大。
zh.significance: 解体标志冷战结束，美国成为唯一超级大国，前苏联地区则经历艰难的政治经济转型。

title: World Wide Web goes public
summary: Tim Berners-Lee, a British scientist at CERN, the European physics laboratory near Geneva, makes his World Wide Web system available to the public over the internet. Proposed in 1989, it links documents on different computers through hyperlinks, using web addresses (URLs), the HTML page format and the HTTP protocol.
significance: After CERN put the technology in the public domain in 1993, the web grew explosively and became the main way people use the internet, transforming communication, commerce and access to information.

zh.title: 万维网向公众开放
zh.summary: 日内瓦附近欧洲核子研究中心的英国科学家蒂姆·伯纳斯-李，将万维网向公众开放。系统于1989年提出，以超链接连接不同计算机上的文件，使用网址、HTML页面格式与HTTP协议。
zh.significance: 1993年欧洲核子研究中心将技术置于公有领域后，万维网迅速发展，改变了通信、商业及获取信息的方式。

title: End of apartheid in South Africa
summary: South Africa holds its first elections in which citizens of all races can vote, ending apartheid, the system of racial segregation and white minority rule in force since 1948. Nelson Mandela, released in 1990 after 27 years in prison, leads the African National Congress to victory and is inaugurated as president in Pretoria.
significance: The largely peaceful transfer of power, followed by a Truth and Reconciliation Commission, made South Africa a constitutional democracy, though deep economic inequality remained.

zh.title: 南非种族隔离制度终结
zh.summary: 南非首次允许所有种族公民共同投票，结束自1948年实行的种族隔离。曾入狱27年的曼德拉率非国大获胜，并在比勒陀利亚就任总统。
zh.significance: 大体和平的权力交接与真相和解委员会，推动南非成为宪政民主国家，但深刻经济不平等仍然存在。

title: Rwandan genocide
summary: After the plane carrying Rwanda's Hutu president Juvénal Habyarimana is shot down, Hutu extremist militias and soldiers begin killing Tutsi and moderate Hutu across the country. In about 100 days an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people, most of them Tutsi, are murdered, many with machetes, until the Tutsi-led Rwandan Patriotic Front defeats the government forces.
significance: The genocide, which the UN and Western powers failed to stop, led to an international tribunal and the doctrine of a 'responsibility to protect', and its aftermath fed wars in neighboring Congo.

zh.title: 卢旺达种族灭绝
zh.summary: 总统哈比亚利马纳的飞机被击落后，胡图极端民兵与军队屠杀图西人和温和胡图人。约一百天内五十万至八十万人遇害，直到卢旺达爱国阵线击败政府军。
zh.significance: 联合国与西方未能阻止屠杀，事件推动国际法庭及“保护责任”理念，其后果又助长邻国刚果战争。

title: Hong Kong returns to China
summary: At midnight, Britain hands Hong Kong to China after more than 150 years of colonial rule, as the lease on most of its territory expires. Under an arrangement called one country, two systems, China promises that the city will keep its own laws, courts and economic system for fifty years.
significance: The handover marked the end of the British Empire in Asia and, for China, the closing of the era that began with the Opium War.

zh.title: 香港回归中国
zh.summary: 随着大部分辖区的租期届满，英国在午夜将殖民统治一百五十余年的香港交还中国。依据“一国两制”安排，中国承诺香港保留自身法律、法院与经济制度五十年。
zh.significance: 交接标志着大英帝国在亚洲统治的终结，对中国而言，也象征鸦片战争开启的时代告一段落。
